h1: Hydraulic shop presses — H-frame workshop and bench presses, 10 to 220 US tons
intro: A hydraulic shop press is the machine every repair shop, truck and equipment dealer and fabricator reaches for several times a day: pressing bearings, bushings and pins, straightening shafts and bar, bending flat bar and short plate, pushing a die for the odd forming job. NovoTech sells two lines in Canada, all on this page, small to large: the premium line, built in Turkey — DPM H-frame shop presses from 33 to 220 US tons with two-speed joystick control, a pressure gauge and a relief valve against overload, and the DPM-K and DK presses whose cylinder travels across the frame on a hand wheel, so the ram meets the work instead of the work being shifted under the ram; and the value line, built in China — the EBP-10T hydraulic bench press for sheet-metal and louver tooling, the EBP-25T motorized workshop press of 28 US tons and the HPP-60 to HPP-160 motorized workshop presses with a moving cylinder, 66 to 176 US tons. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. For die work and production, see the H-frame and C-frame presses; for beams and plate, the straightening presses. Parts, installation and service from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: What tonnage shop press do I need?
faq.a: Most truck, equipment and fabrication shops run a 66 – 110 US ton press (DPM 1040-60 to DPM 1570-100, or the value-line HPP-60 and HPP-100): enough for pressing bearings and bushings, straightening shafts to Ø3″ and bending flat bar. Go to 165 – 220 US tons for large bearings, track pins, heavy shafts and forming plate. Beams and plate that need a moving ram are on the straightening press page.

faq.q: What do the model numbers mean — DPM 1040-60?
faq.a: The first number is the clear working width between the columns in millimetres (1040 mm = 40.9″) and the second the press force in metric tons (60 t = 66 US tons). A 1570-100 press is 61.8″ wide at 110 US tons.

On the DPM-K and DK the cylinder head travels across the frame on a hand wheel, so the ram comes to the work — a long shaft, a frame rail or a plate stays clamped while you straighten it point by point instead of shifting the part under a fixed ram. The DK series adds a wider 61.8″ – 74.8″ frame. The value-line HPP presses also have a cylinder that moves across the frame.

faq.q: Hand pump, foot pedal or joystick?
faq.a: The DPM and DPM-K presses come with two-speed joystick control; a hand pump for fine pressing, a foot pedal and a limit switch that stops the stroke at a set height are options. The value-line HPP presses pair the motorized two-step unit with a double-acting hand pump for fine positioning, and the EBP-25T has infinitely variable pressure and speed.

faq.q: What is the EBP-10T bench press for?
faq.a: The sheet-metal and HVAC shop: its 25″ throat and 6″ tool opening take the industry-standard bench and louver press tooling, so it punches round, square and oblong holes, punches and flares or beads, cuts louvers, notches corners, bends 90° in 3/8″ mild steel and shears 16 ga — and it works as a hydraulic arbor press as well.

The premium-line shop and production presses are built in Turkey with European hydraulics and Siemens controls, for daily production work, straightening lines and custom sizes. The value-line presses are built in China for the repair shop, the maintenance department and lighter production — the same tonnages at a lower price, with built-on or separate power units.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
